newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Police arrest driver after Bosnia convoy incident.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest driver after Bosnia convoy incident.

text.p: Bosnian Croat police on Monday arrested a Croat driver who rammed a security vehicle in a convoy carrying Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic across southern Bosnia, the Croatian state news agency HINA reported.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was in charge of security for a six-vehicle convoy transporting Izetbegovic, Bosnian Federation president Kresimir Zubak and the OSCE's head of mission in Bosnia, Robert Frowick.
All three men were headed to the Croatian port of Split for a flight to Monday's OSCE summit in Lisbon.
The incident occurred about 20 km (12 miles) south of Mostar, near Capljina.
Hina said Mostar police arrested the driver, Ivan Puljic, after the incident. A police statement said he was currently receiving treatment at a local hospital and the case was being investigated.
OSCE spokesman Johan Verheyden told reporters the Croat, who was driving a truck, repeatedly tried to break into the convoy and ignored warnings to desist.
He said an OSCE security car had given Puljic clear warnings to back off, but Mostar police said Puljic realised the convoy was carrying important politicians only "after force was used".
"Then he started ramming the chase car in its rear. Once more the OSCE security detail warned the driver to keep his distance but the driver gave no heed to the warning," Verheyden said in Sarajevo.

He said the bodyguard waved his Uzi submachine gun at the Croat driver "to show him that decisive action could be taken." The OSCE guard then "opened fire on the truck, wounding its driver in the shoulder," the spokesman explained.

"We have no details so far why he tried to break into the convoy. We think it is more a case of driver madness...than a direct attack on the presidents or on Ambassador Frowick. So far we have no details whether the man was armed."
Virtually all top Bosnian officials and foreign diplomats travel with personal security details.
In a country awash with weapons and still nursing blood grudges from 43 months of war, their job is to act decisively to protect the lives of their charges.
Verheyden said Frowick, Izetbegovic and Zubak -- himself a Croat -- were completely satisfied with the bodyguard's actions.
